name: First-Party and Bust-Out Fraud
description: Customers or organised groups obtain credit with no intent to repay, or build up credit lines and then max them out and vanish. First-party fraud may also include exaggerated hardship or false disputes.

sources.text: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (specify year, e.g. 2025)
FinCEN, advisories on loan and credit fraud (general)
FATF, guidance on proceeds of fraud (general)

indicators.name: Sudden utilisation spike to limit after a period of low use
indicators.canon: Sudden credit utilisation spike then bust-out
indicators.desc: Credit builds up and is then rapidly utilised to limit or cashed out after a period of low use.
indicators.ctx: Balances move from low to maximum across cards or lines within days.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Cash advances and purchases of resaleable goods
indicators.canon: Cash advances and purchases of resaleable goods
indicators.desc: Heavy use of cash advances, gift cards and high-resale items near the credit limit.
indicators.ctx: Heavy use of cash advances, gift cards and high-resale items near the credit limit.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Rapid payments from third-party or overdrawn accounts to inflate limits
indicators.canon: Rapid payments from third-party or overdrawn accounts to inflate limits
indicators.desc: Payments that bounce or are reversed after credit is restored.
indicators.ctx: Payments that bounce or are reversed after credit is restored.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Multiple linked accounts opened across lenders
indicators.canon: Shared device, contact or address data across many applicants or senders
indicators.desc: The same device fingerprint, IP, phone, email or address appears across many applications, claims or apparent customers.
indicators.ctx: Shared addresses or phones across applicants hitting many lenders.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Customer unreachable after account reaches limit
indicators.canon: Customer unreachable after account reaches limit
indicators.desc: Contact details become invalid and the customer ceases engagement.
indicators.ctx: Contact details become invalid and the customer ceases engagement.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Stated income or employer not verifiable
indicators.canon: Stated income or employer not verifiable
indicators.desc: Application cites employer or income that cannot be confirmed.
indicators.ctx: Application cites employer or income that cannot be confirmed.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Increased use of merchants known for transaction laundering
indicators.desc: A merchant processes sales for undisclosed businesses, or customers use merchants whose profile suggests card-cash-out or third-party processing.
indicators.ctx: Use at merchants with risky profiles suggesting cash-out.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Early limit increase requests
indicators.desc: Repeated and quickly sought limit increases soon after account opening.
indicators.ctx: Repeated and quickly sought limit increases soon after account opening.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Customer disputes legitimate transactions after use
indicators.desc: Customer falsely claims non-receipt or unauthorised use for transactions they made, often from their own device.
indicators.ctx: False claims of non-receipt or unauthorised use.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)
